text:
diego: heads-up: rvq onboarding in staging shows overall NDCG@10 +1.4% but MRR@5 for transactional product-code queries (regex: [A-Z]{2}\d{3}) down -5.4%. pasting quick slice.

anika: product-code slice? is that the sku-like queries we talked about?

diego: yes. table from eval-run-pt-09:
```
metric       overall   product_code   natural_lang
NDCG@10      +1.4%     +0.6%          +1.9%
MRR@5        -0.3%     -5.4%          +0.8%
Top1_rate    -0.7pp   -7.9pp         -0.1pp
```
changes that came with rvq: canonical_query_expansion enabled (normalizes "AB123" -> "ab-123"), aggressive punctuation_strip, and switched candidate_cache_key to include quant_variant tag. Also int8 PTQ landed.

fen: canonical expansion sounds like the likely suspect. For code-like queries we want exact token preservation. Does expansion insert hyphen or change order?

diego: it lowercases and inserts a hyphen between alpha and numeric runs. we did this to unify vendor variants like "AB123" vs "ab-123" but it appears to break direct-string-match behavior.

anika: also that candidate_cache_key change could cause a stale cache effect: if cached candidate embeddings were produced with previous model variant, and now keys include quant tag, we might be hitting cold cache or mismatched candidates leading to score shifts.

eval-bot: queued fast ablation: (A) canonical_expansion=off (B) punctuation_strip=off (C) candidate_cache_key=legacy (D) quant=fp16. Command: 
```
./eval_rerank --model rvq --dataset holdout_txn --slices product_code \\
  --canonical {on,off} --punct_strip {on,off} --cache_key {new,legacy} --quant {int8,fp16}
```
ETA ~12m.

fen: also collect exact_string_match_rate and cache_hit_rate in the results. If exact matches drop with canonical=on that's the smoking gun.

eval-bot: job 9123 started.

ops-bot: note: Dedicated rollout paused for rvq until triage completes.

eval-bot: job 9123 finished. quick deltas vs baseline (legacy config):
- A (canonical=off, punct_strip=on, cache_key=new, quant=int8): product_code MRR delta = +4.8% (nearly recovered)
- B (canonical=on, punct_strip=off, cache_key=new, quant=int8): product_code MRR delta = +1.2% (partial recovery)
- C (canonical=on, punct_strip=on, cache_key=legacy, quant=int8): product_code MRR delta = +2.0%
- D (canonical=off, punct_strip=off, cache_key=legacy, quant=fp16): product_code MRR delta = +5.6% (full recovery)
additional metrics: exact_string_match_rate for product_code slice dropped -8.7pp with canonical=on; cache_hit_rate improved when using legacy cache_key for previously warmed candidates.

anika: tl;dr: canonical expansion is the primary driver (breaks exact matches), punctuation_strip contributes, and cache_key change caused cold/miss behavior that amplified the effect for high-volume SKUs. quant (int8) adds a small ~0.6-1.0pp penalty but not primary.

fen: action items: 1) revert canonical expansion for queries matching SKU regex (low-risk rule) 2) revert cache_key change so candidate cache warms across model variants during rollouts (or ensure warm migration) 3) keep punctuation_strip off for short alphanumeric tokens.

diego: agree. I'll ship a config patch that gates canonical_expansion off for regex ^[A-Z]{2}\d{3}$ and change cache_key back to legacy. Will queue a 5% A/B for 3h and monitor top1/mrr/exact_match. rollout doc: https://go/rollout/rvq-sku-exception

ops-bot: Rollout created: rvq-sku-exception (5% -> 25% after 3h if metrics stable). Safety flag: hold Dedicated until A/B green.

eval-bot: adding a small offline test in PR CI to assert exact_string_match_rate on product_code slice does not drop >1pp for token-normalizer changes.

anika: also file a follow-up: consider a smarter canonicalization that preserves exact-match tokens for short alnum spans and only canonicalizes long vendor names. ticket: https://go/issue/infra/31415

diego: thanks all. learned: canonicalizers and cache-key churn can interact to make exact-match-heavy slices (transactional/skus/code-search) fail badly even when overall NDCG looks fine. will post A/B numbers here.
